function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and can include optional query parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

search.description: Query parameter to search for a specific term.

limit.description: Query parameter to limit the number of results.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers to include in the request as key-value pairs.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Authorization.description: Authorization credentials for connecting to the resource.

timeout.description: The amount of time to wait for a server response, in seconds. This is a float type value.

I’m not aware of any source reporting **total** Apple Inc. revenue at $21 billion—most publicly‑available filings show far higher totals.  
For example:

| Period | Total Net Sales / Revenue |
|--------|---------------------------|
| Fiscal year FY23 (ended Sep 30 2023) | ≈ \$383 billion |
| Quarter ending Mar 31 2024 (Q1 24) | ≈ \$95 billion |

Even when looking at individual segments, the largest one—the *iPhone* business—is usually around \$55–65 billion per fiscal year, still well above \$21 billion.

If your figure refers to a particular sub‑segment, region, or a different metric (e.g., operating income), let me know so I can dig up the exact data. Otherwise, it’s possible there’s been a mix‑up between “revenue” and another financial measure such as profit margin, cash flow, or a smaller subsidiary’s earnings.
